group.title: Home and town
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A set of rooms for living in, in a larger building.
examples: They live in a small {apartment} on the third floor.
wrong: An apartment is a field where cows eat grass.

words.meaning: Things like tables, chairs and beds.
examples: We bought new {furniture} for the living room.
wrong: Furniture is a kind of vegetable.

words.meaning: A long soft seat for two or three people.
examples: We watched television on the {sofa}.
wrong: A sofa is a place where you wash your hands.

words.meaning: A machine that keeps food cold.
examples: Put the milk in the {fridge}.
wrong: A fridge is a machine that keeps food very hot.

words.meaning: A closed box that heats food.
examples: Bake the cake in the {oven} for forty minutes.
wrong: An oven is a machine that makes food cold.

words.meaning: A flat board on a wall where you put things.
examples: Put the books on the {shelf}.
wrong: A shelf is a kind of window.

words.meaning: A thick cover for a floor.
examples: The children play on the soft {carpet}.
wrong: A carpet is a thin cover for a window.

words.meaning: A light that you can move.
examples: He turned on the {lamp} to read.
wrong: A lamp is a machine that keeps food cold.

words.meaning: The surface you walk on inside a room.
examples: The cat sleeps on the {floor}.
wrong: The floor is the top part of a room.

words.meaning: The surface above your head in a room.
examples: There is a big light on the {ceiling}.
wrong: The ceiling is the surface that you walk on.

words.meaning: A side of a room or a building.
examples: A picture hangs on the {wall}.
wrong: A wall is a flat piece of wood on the floor.

words.meaning: A small platform outside an upstairs window.
examples: We have breakfast on the {balcony}.
wrong: A balcony is a room under the ground.

words.meaning: Steps that go from one floor to another.
examples: I walked up the {stairs} to the fourth floor.
wrong: Stairs is a machine that carries people up and down by itself.

words.meaning: A machine that carries people up and down in a building.
examples: We took the {elevator} to the tenth floor.
wrong: An elevator is a staircase made of glass.

words.meaning: A person who owns a house and rents it to others.
examples: Our {landlord} fixed the broken door.
wrong: A landlord is a person who rents a house from someone else.

words.meaning: Money you pay to live in a place that belongs to someone else.
examples: The {rent} for this apartment is $800 a month.
wrong: Rent is the money a landlord pays to the tenant.

words.meaning: To fix something that is broken.
examples: He will {repair} my bicycle tomorrow.
wrong: I repair a toy by throwing it away.

words.meaning: Power that makes lights and machines work.
examples: The {electricity} went off during the storm.
wrong: Electricity is a hot drink.

words.meaning: A sound, especially a loud or unpleasant one.
examples: The {noise} from the street kept me awake.
wrong: Noise is the quiet feeling you have in an empty room.

words.meaning: Making little or no noise.
examples: The library is very {quiet}.
wrong: The market was quiet because hundreds of people were shouting.

words.meaning: Full of people.
examples: The train was too {crowded}, so I stood.
wrong: The beach was crowded, and I was alone with nobody there.

words.meaning: Cars and other vehicles moving along a road.
examples: There was a lot of {traffic} on the way to work.
wrong: Traffic is a kind of food you eat at lunch.

words.meaning: A path at the side of a road where people walk.
examples: Please walk on the {sidewalk}.
wrong: A sidewalk is the middle part of the road for cars.

words.meaning: The place where two streets or two walls meet.
examples: The bakery is on the {corner}.
wrong: A corner is a long straight road.

words.meaning: A large shop that sells food and other things for the home.
examples: I buy milk at the {supermarket}.
wrong: A supermarket is a small shop that sells only stamps.

words.meaning: The details of where someone lives or works.
examples: Please write your {address} on the form.
wrong: An address is a person who lives near you.

words.meaning: Something wrapped up to be sent or carried.
examples: A {package} arrived this morning.
wrong: A package is an empty room without a door.

words.meaning: An area of a town and the people who live there.
examples: I like my quiet {neighborhood}.
wrong: A neighborhood is a large country with many cities.

words.meaning: Pleasant to sit in or wear; relaxed.
examples: This bed is very {comfortable}.
wrong: This chair is comfortable because it hurts my back.

words.meaning: Of the present time; new in style.
examples: They live in a {modern} house with a large kitchen.
wrong: The castle is modern because it was built a thousand years ago.

words.meaning: Warm and comfortable in a pleasant, small way.
examples: We spent a {cozy} evening by the fire.
wrong: The cold, empty room felt very cozy.

words.meaning: Making a lot of sound.
examples: The classroom was {noisy} before the teacher came.
wrong: The library is noisy because everyone is silent.

words.meaning: Not in danger; not likely to cause harm.
examples: It is {safe} to walk here at night.
wrong: The road is safe because cars drive very fast and no one looks.

words.meaning: Not clean.
examples: Your shoes are {dirty}; please wash them.
wrong: The towel is dirty, so it is clean.

words.meaning: Neat; with everything in its place.
examples: Her room is always {tidy}.
wrong: The room is tidy because things are on the floor.

words.meaning: To go to live in a different place.
examples: We will {move} to a new house in May.
wrong: We move when we stay in the same house for ten years.

words.meaning: To make a place look nice with paint or objects.
examples: We will {decorate} the room with pictures.
wrong: I decorate the room by taking everything away.

words.meaning: A building where you keep a car.
examples: He parks the car in the {garage}.
wrong: A garage is a place where you cook dinner.

words.meaning: A room with a bath or shower.
examples: She is washing her hands in the {bathroom}.
wrong: A bathroom is a room where we cook breakfast.

words.meaning: A piece of cloth for drying your body.
examples: Use a clean {towel} after your shower.
wrong: A towel is a thing that you wear on your feet.
